idiom_name: protocol + struct service; Fluent db.transaction closure
implementation_notes: Protocol-oriented Swift replaces the service class with a protocol of operations and a struct implementation, with dependencies injected through the initialiser or registered in the framework's service container (Vapor's Application storage). The transaction boundary is a closure rather than an annotation: Fluent's db.transaction { transaction in ... } runs the body inside a transaction and rolls it back when the closure throws, so the operation method and its unit of work are the same block. The reference-typed class service is still justified when the service must hold shared mutable state (a cache, an open connection) that value semantics would copy per use rather than share.
pitfalls: Every query inside the closure must use the transaction's database parameter; using the outer db escapes the transaction.
The closure rolls back only when it throws - swallowing the error inside commits nothing and hides the failure.
Services are value types: a struct's mutable cache is copied per use, not shared - inject a reference type or actor for shared state.
